title: Confirming the Presence of Neurapraxia and Its Potential for Immediate Reversal by Novel Diagnostic and Therapeutic Ultrasound-Guided Hydrodissection Using 5% Dextrose in Water Without Local Anesthetic: Application in a Case of Acute Radial Nerve Palsy
content: Introduction: Radial nerve palsy, often manifesting as wrist drop, is a peripheral neuropathy typically resulting from compression. While conservative management is often employed, recovery can be prolonged. It has been commonly taught that cases like this involve a conduction block, which significantly limits diagnostic physical examination or electrodiagnosis. However, if hydrodissection (HD) can immediately restore function, it may indicate that the injury is merely neurapraxia, and highlight its degree of reversibility, profoundly influencing the course of recovery. We present a case of acute radial nerve palsy successfully treated with ultrasound-guided (US-guided) HD. Case Presentation: A 54-year-old woman with diabetes presented with sudden onset of left wrist drop with no apparent trauma. Physical examination revealed an inability to actively extend her wrist, and plain radiographs were unremarkable. Given the clinical presentation suggestive of radial nerve palsy, US-guided HD was performed at the proximal spiral groove using 50 mL of 5% dextrose in water (D5W) with no local anesthetic (LA). Immediate post-procedural assessment showed marked improvement in wrist extension. At one-month follow-up, the patient reported complete resolution of wrist drop and restoration of normal daily activities, with no loss of work, which was maintained at a three-month telephone review. Electrodiagnostic studies were not performed due to the retrospective nature of this case report. Discussion: This case demonstrates the potential for rapid and nearly complete clinical recovery from acute compressive radial nerve palsy following a single US-guided HD injection using D5W without LA, confirming the presence of neuropraxia and its nearly complete reversibility. However, an electromyogram (EMG) showing the pattern of motor fiber recruitment post injection was not available. Conclusion: US-guided HD with D5W with no LA may be a promising therapeutic option for selected patients with acute compressive radial nerve palsy. However, further research - including controlled trials and electrodiagnostic confirmation - is needed to determine the frequency in which immediate diagnostic and therapeutic HD with D5W is expected to be therapeutically valuable in altering function and optimizing rehabilitation
